gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-dives-akuru: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly climbs to its capitals. Its crossbars match the stems in thickness, so it earns its keep big and brief, while Noto Serif Dives Akuru brings the softly swelling strokes of a worn felt marker.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Gugi cuts its terminals open so the counters flow outward, with every curve matching its stems like a marker line. Noto Serif Dogra, a text serif, then adds gentle thickening at the shoulders, giving the page a faint crayon-on-rough-paper texture beneath.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-ethiopic: Gugi is a display face with tall lowercase and curves that turn corners without any pressure swell, all bold and distinctive. Noto Serif Ethiopic settles into solid word blocks.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-georgian: Chunky, tall and unmistakably marker-drawn. Gugi keeps its line width constant from start to finish, and Noto Serif Georgian trades that for tightly coiled lowercase with mid-level stroke contrast, a literary, authoritative texture the heading never attempts.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-grantha: Gugi brings bowls as heavy as its stems. Noto Serif Grantha, a text serif, follows with thin strokes of respectable weight and oversized small letters, a tempered contrast that carries a long passage without jolting.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-gujarati: Bold marker strokes, tall lowercase, zero fuss. Gugi gives every stroke the same gauge, while Noto Serif Gujarati lightens its thin strokes slightly and eases its joins, so the display heading and the serif text feel bookish beneath it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi: Gugi's monoline skeleton and open-cut terminals make its tall lowercase instantly distinctive and bold at display size. Noto Serif Gurmukhi, a classic serif, handles the quieter work.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-hebrew: Noto Serif Hebrew reads with a tall, sturdy body and lightly pronounced swelling in each rounded letter, authoritative and classic. Under Gugi's uniform-heft diagonals, a long passage stays steady.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Noto Serif Kannada reads big-countered and traditional, literary in tone. Gugi's compass-pencil consistency sits above it, so give the Kannada body a comfortable size to let its robust downstrokes and slender turns breathe.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Noto Serif Khmer is a classic, authoritative serif with tall lowercase and only mild hairline thinning at its curves. And Gugi, bold and thick-only in its outlines, supplies the loud counterpoint that makes the two distinct.
